fields.q1: What components currently exist in the DeltaGraph codebase at scripts/deltagraph/?
fields.a1: Todas las capas del CKG: domain/ (4 archivos: knowledge_graph.py con KnowledgeNode/KnowledgeEdge/KnowledgeGraph, models.py con NodeType/EdgeType, errors.py, graph.py), application/ (5 archivos: ckg.py con CodeKnowledgeGraph, context.py, detection.py, migration.py, query.py), infrastructure/ (4 archivos: repository.py con JsonRepository, scanners.py con ImportScanner/LayerScanner/SymbolScanner/QltyScanner, qlty.py, schema.py), y __init__.py con API publica. Total: 17 archivos con ~1349 lineas. ~10 consumers externos en scripts/tasks/, side_effects/, _walker/commands.py. Especial: ckg_persist.py llama a save_knowledge_nodes() pero el metodo real es save_nodes() - bug a corregir.
fields.q2: What impact does the DeltaGraph migration have on each component and its consumers?
fields.a2: Internas: domain no tiene dependencias externas. Application (ckg.py) importa de _walker/shared/cognitive_graph.py (CognitiveGraph facade) y de _walker/shared/path_resolver. Infrastructure (repository.py) usa json.gz persistence. Externas: scripts/tasks/* (5 archivos), side_effects/ckg_persist.py, scripts/_walker/commands.py, scripts/bkg/. NO tiene dependencias del CPG - solo de CognitiveGraph y path_resolver. Importante: CKG ya usa CognitiveGraph como capa de datos (a traves de _walker/shared/cognitive_graph.py), lo que facilitara la futura TASK-010.
fields.q3: What implementation approach is recommended for a safe DeltaGraph migration?
fields.a3: Enfoque en 6 pasos: 1) Crear features/cognitive_knowledge/{domain,application,infrastructure}/, 2) Migrar domain (sin dependencias externas), 3) Migrar infrastructure (repository y scanners), 4) Migrar application (ckg.py, context, detection, migration, query), 5) Crear shim en scripts/ckg/__init__.py con sys.modules forwarding (como en CPG), 6) Corregir bug en side_effects/ckg_persist.py: save_knowledge_nodes -> save_nodes. Verificar con import tests y CognitiveGraph.query(). Riesgo: ckg.py ya importa CognitiveGraph directamente - asegurar que la ruta se actualice a libs/ o features/.

fields.evidence: DeltaGraph migration design approved: 11 files, 3 layers (domain, application, infrastructure), standalone feature sin dependencias externas, 5-step migration con shim (mismo patrón probado en TASK-001/002/003). Riesgo bajo.

fields.q1: All layers of scripts/deltagraph/ will be affected: domain/ (2 files: __init__.py, models.py with TokenIndex, IndexEntry dataclasses), application/ (3 files: __init__.py, index_service.py with index_sprint/index_all, search_service.py with search_tasks/search_by_source), infrastructure/ (2 files: __init__.py, repository.py with save_index/load_index to data/delta.json.gz), and __init__.py (public API: DeltaGraphService with methods index_sprint, index_all, search, clear). Total: 11 files (~489 lines). ~6 external consumers: CognitiveGraph facade in _walker/shared/cognitive_graph.py, context providers in _walker/workflow_engine/context/providers.py, QueryDeltaGraphUseCase, side_effects update_delta_graph, _walker/commands.py cmd_deltagraph, and _internal/graph.py (legacy DeltaGraph class). DeltaGraph has ZERO dependencies on CPG or CKG — it is fully independent.
fields.q2: Internal dependencies: domain has no external deps (only stdlib dataclasses). Application depends only on domain/models.py (TokenIndex, IndexEntry). Infrastructure depends on domain/models.py and stdlib gzip/json. The public API (DeltaGraphService) orchestrates application + infrastructure. External consumers: CognitiveGraph facade imports DeltaGraphService for delta search handler, context/providers.py formats DeltaGraph results for LLM context, side_effects.py has update_delta_graph/restore_delta_graph compensation, QueryDeltaGraphUseCase queries via CognitiveGraph, commands.py has cmd_deltagraph (legacy). NO circular dependencies. NO dependency on CPG, CKG, or other features — DeltaGraph is a standalone text index shared across the engine.
fields.q3: Recommended approach in 5 steps (proven pattern from TASK-001/002/003): 1) Create features/delta_tracking/{domain,application,infrastructure}/ with __init__.py, 2) Migrate domain first (models.py with TokenIndex, IndexEntry — zero external deps), 3) Migrate infrastructure (repository.py with gzip save/load to data/delta.json.gz), 4) Migrate application (index_service.py, search_service.py), 5) Create shim in scripts/deltagraph/__init__.py with sys.modules forwarding (same pattern as CPG and CKG). Verify with: from features.delta_tracking import DeltaGraphService. Risk: low — DeltaGraph is independent with no cross-feature dependencies. The index data (data/delta.json.gz) must be preserved during migration.

submitted_fields.q1: Which layers/modules of workflow-engine will be affected by the migration to features/?
submitted_fields.a1: Todas las capas del engine se ven afectadas: domain (7 modulos: models, services, errors, session, state, registry, project_registry), application (5 modulos: use_cases, orchestrator, workflow_api, context_resolver, query_use_cases), infrastructure (5 modulos: repositories, task_registry, side_effects, trace_log, config), context/ (providers, composer), y bootstrap.py. Ninguna otra feature se ve afectada directamente porque el shim en _walker/__init__.py re-exportara todo desde features.workflow_engine.
submitted_fields.q2: What internal and external dependencies exist for the workflow-engine?
submitted_fields.a2: Internas: interface (CLI commands) depende de application (orchestrator, use_cases) que depende de domain (models, services). Infrastructure (repositories, task_registry, side_effects) depende de domain. Externas: workflow-engine depende de libs/infrastructure via path_resolver para resolucion de rutas. CLI, CPG, CKG y otras features dependen de workflow-engine via sus puertos definidos en domain. No hay dependencias circulares.
submitted_fields.q3: What is the main implementation risk and how do we mitigate it?
submitted_fields.a3: Riesgo principal: imports rotos por cambio de ruta de _walker.workflow_engine.xxx a features.workflow_engine.xxx. Hay ~40 archivos importando de _walker.workflow_engine. Mitigacion: 1) shim en _walker/__init__.py que re-exporta todo, 2) migracion gradual archivo por archivo, 3) verificar con import tests despues de cada migracion, 4) mantener ambos paths funcionales hasta completar todas las tareas del sprint.

submitted_fields.feedback: TASK-002 CPG migration aprobada. 19 archivos, 14 consumers, shim en scripts/cpg/__init__.py. Proceder a implementacion.

submitted_fields.q1: Which layers/modules of scripts/cpg/ will be affected by the migration to features/code-analysis/?
submitted_fields.a1: Todas las capas del CPG se ven afectadas: domain (5 modulos: graph, query, analysis, metrics), application (5 modulos: build_service, query_service, bug_service, review_service, query), infrastructure (6 modulos: repository, sg_adapter, ast_grep_adapter, ast_grep_calls, filters, metrics), y __init__py (API publica: CPGBuilder, CpgQueryService). Total: 19 archivos, ~2819 lineas. ~25 imports externos en scripts/tasks/ y _walker/commands.py necesitan shim. Ninguna otra feature se ve afectada porque scripts/cpg/__init__py re-exportara todo desde features.code_analysis.
submitted_fields.q2: What are the internal and external dependencies of scripts/cpg/?
submitted_fields.a2: Internas: domain (graph, query, analysis, metrics) no tiene dependencias externas - es el core puro. Application (build, query, bug, review) depende de domain. Infrastructure (repository, sg_adapter, ast_grep) depende de domain y de libs/shared para path_resolver. Externas hay ~25 imports: scripts/tasks/* (8 archivos), scripts/_walker/commands.py (CPGBuilder, CpgQueryService), scripts/_walker/shared/cognitive_graph.py (CpgFileRepository), scripts/side_effects/cpg_updates.py (CPGBuilder). No hay dependencias circulares.
submitted_fields.q3: What is the main implementation risk and how do we mitigate it?
submitted_fields.a3: Riesgo principal: ~25 imports rotos por cambio de ruta de scripts/cpg/xxx a features.code_analysis.xxx. Mitigacion: 1) Shim en scripts/cpg/__init__.py que re-exporta todo desde features.code_analysis, 2) Migracion gradual empezando por domain (sin deps externas), 3) Verificar con import tests: python3 -c from features.code_analysis import CPGBuilder, 4) Preservar CPG index existente (no regenerar desde cero). Riesgo secundario: si el CPGBuilder se rompe, walker3 status/submit/query dejarian de funcionar. Mitigacion: CPG stats post-migracion para verificar mismo numero de nodos/edges.

submitted_fields.evidence: Diseno correcto, migracion gradual con shim, sin dependencias circulares. Proceder a ANALYZE

submitted_fields.q1: What components currently exist in the CPG codebase at scripts/cpg/?
submitted_fields.a1: Existen 19 archivos en 4 capas: domain/ (5: graph.py con Node/Edge/Graph dataclasses, query.py con Query/Filter, analysis.py con BugFinding/DeadCodeCandidate, metrics.py con ReviewResult/ProjectMetrics), application/ (5: build_service.py con BuildGraphUseCase pipeline sg outline→CFG→DFG, query_service.py con grep/read/structured access, bug_service.py con dead code y security scan, review_service.py con code review metrics, query.py atajo), infrastructure/ (6: repository.py con CpgFileRepository para load/save cpg.json.gz, sg_adapter con run_outline/parse_outline, ast_grep_adapter, ast_grep_calls para CFG/DFG scan, filters, metrics), y __init__.py (API publica: CPGBuilder + CpgQueryService). Total ~2819 lineas de codigo funcional.
submitted_fields.q2: What impact does the CPG migration have on each component and its consumers?
submitted_fields.a2: Impacto nulo en logica de negocio: domain no cambia (no tiene imports externos). Application cambia imports de scripts.cpg.xxx a features.code_analysis.xxx. Infrastructure cambia imports de scripts/shared a libs. El shim en scripts/cpg/__init__.py re-exporta CPGBuilder y CpgQueryService para ~25 consumers externos: scripts/tasks/* (8 archivos), scripts/_walker/commands.py, scripts/_walker/shared/cognitive_graph.py, scripts/side_effects/cpg_updates.py. Sin impacto en walker3 commands porque usan CPGBuilder via __init__.py que tendra shim.
submitted_fields.q3: What implementation approach is recommended for a safe CPG migration?
submitted_fields.a3: Enfoque en 5 pasos probado en TASK-001: 1) Crear features/code-analysis/{domain,application,infrastructure}/ con __init__.py, 2) Migrar domain primero (sin dependencias externas), 3) Migrar infrastructure (repository necesita path_resolver de libs), 4) Migrar application (depende de domain e infrastructure), 5) Crear shim en scripts/cpg/__init__.py. Verificar con python3 -c from features.code_analysis import CPGBuilder. Verificar CPG stats post-migracion (mismo num nodos/edges). Riesgo principal: preservar indice CPG existente (no regenerar).

submitted_fields.a1: Todas las capas del CKG: domain/ (4 archivos: knowledge_graph.py con KnowledgeNode/KnowledgeEdge/KnowledgeGraph, models.py con NodeType/EdgeType, errors.py, graph.py), application/ (5 archivos: ckg.py con CodeKnowledgeGraph, context.py, detection.py, migration.py, query.py), infrastructure/ (4 archivos: repository.py con JsonRepository, scanners.py con ImportScanner/LayerScanner/SymbolScanner/QltyScanner, qlty.py, schema.py), y __init__.py con API publica. Total: 17 archivos con ~1349 lineas. ~10 consumers externos en scripts/tasks/, side_effects/, _walker/commands.py. submitted_fields.q2: What dependencies does the CKG have on other modules and CognitiveGraph?

Infrastructure (repository.py) usa json.gz persistence. Externas: scripts/tasks/* (5 archivos), side_effects/ckg_persist.py, scripts/_walker/commands.py, scripts/bkg/. submitted_fields.q3: What is the recommended migration approach for CKG including the CognitiveGraph integration?

Verificar con import tests y CognitiveGraph.query(). Riesgo: ckg.py ya importa CognitiveGraph directamente - asegurar que la ruta se actualice a libs/ o features/.

submitted_fields.q1: All layers of scripts/deltagraph/ will be affected: domain/ (2 files: __init__.py, models.py with TokenIndex, IndexEntry dataclasses), application/ (3 files: __init__.py, index_service.py with index_sprint/index_all, search_service.py with search_tasks/search_by_source), infrastructure/ (2 files: __init__.py, repository.py with save_index/load_index to data/delta.json.gz), and __init__.py (public API: DeltaGraphService with methods index_sprint, index_all, search, clear). Total: 11 files (~489 lines). ~6 external consumers: CognitiveGraph facade in _walker/shared/cognitive_graph.py, context providers in _walker/workflow_engine/context/providers.py, QueryDeltaGraphUseCase, side_effects update_delta_graph, _walker/commands.py cmd_deltagraph, and _internal/graph.py (legacy DeltaGraph class). DeltaGraph has ZERO dependencies on CPG or CKG — it is fully independent.
submitted_fields.q2: Internal dependencies: domain has no external deps (only stdlib dataclasses). Application depends only on domain/models.py (TokenIndex, IndexEntry). Infrastructure depends on domain/models.py and stdlib gzip/json. The public API (DeltaGraphService) orchestrates application + infrastructure. External consumers: CognitiveGraph facade imports DeltaGraphService for delta search handler, context/providers.py formats DeltaGraph results for LLM context, side_effects.py has update_delta_graph/restore_delta_graph compensation, QueryDeltaGraphUseCase queries via CognitiveGraph, commands.py has cmd_deltagraph (legacy). NO circular dependencies. NO dependency on CPG, CKG, or other features — DeltaGraph is a standalone text index shared across the engine.
submitted_fields.q3: Recommended approach in 5 steps (proven pattern from TASK-001/002/003): 1) Create features/delta_tracking/{domain,application,infrastructure}/ with __init__.py, 2) Migrate domain first (models.py with TokenIndex, IndexEntry — zero external deps), 3) Migrate infrastructure (repository.py with gzip save/load to data/delta.json.gz), 4) Migrate application (index_service.py, search_service.py), 5) Create shim in scripts/deltagraph/__init__.py with sys.modules forwarding (same pattern as CPG and CKG). Verify with: from features.delta_tracking import DeltaGraphService. Risk: low — DeltaGraph is independent with no cross-feature dependencies. The index data (data/delta.json.gz) must be preserved during migration.
